newsitem.title: USA: Semiconductor equipment May book-to-bill down.
newsitem.headline: Semiconductor equipment May book-to-bill down.

text.p: The North American semiconductor equipment book-to-bill ratio fell to 1.09 for May from a revised ratio of 1.10 for April as shipment growth made a slight advance against booking growth rates, a trade group said Tuesday.

The closely watched ratio measures the health of companies that supply chipmakers with manufacturing equipment. A book-to-bill of 1.10 means $110 in orders were received for each $100 worth of products shipped.

The figure was reported by Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International, which also noted that three-month average shipments rose in May for the third straight month, to $1.3 billion, 4.8 percent above the April level of $1.3 billion.
The trade group said shipment levels for equipment are now only three percent below the $1.4 billion point of May 1996.

"Shipments of semiconductor equipment by North American-based manufacturers to worldwide markets continued on a path of steady recovery during May," SEMI principal analyst Dick Greene said in a statement issued Tuesday evening.
"Companies are definitely buying, perhaps not so much for capacity expansion, but for refurbishment and certainly for technology upgrades."
SEMI said total equipment order input also continued to grow in May to $1.4 billion, with three-month average bookings rising 3.6 percent above April levels.
It said that was the third straight monthly advance in orders, which are now more than 20 percent above the same month of 1996.
